_comment: Demo script for the booth (design section 5.4). One persona, seven past chats from November and December 2026, and four demo questions dated 2027-01-06 (DEMO_DATE in deploy/.env, a Wednesday). Every question needs facts from two or three different chats, so the no-memory answer can only be generic. Each turn is short and states one fact in words close to the question that needs it, and turns that carry no fact are left out: the search ranks single turns by embedding similarity, and a chatty turn on the same topic outranks the fact (issue 45, company measurement of 2026-10-28). Dates carry the Las Vegas offset; turns are one minute apart. The expected phrases are checked by scripts/demo_check.py against the top-k memories.

turns.content: My daughter Mia has a peanut allergy, so every meal and every party menu at our house has to be peanut-free. Her school asked for safe lunch ideas. Can you help?

Of course. Peanut-free lunches for Mia: turkey and cheese roll-ups with apple slices, pasta salad with cherry tomatoes and mozzarella, a bean and cheese quesadilla, and rice balls with cucumber. Always check labels for 'may contain peanuts'.
She will eat anything with pasta, but she refuses mushrooms. Keep that in mind for any food you plan for her.
Noted: for Mia, pasta is always welcome, mushrooms are out, and nothing with peanuts.
Mia turns 7 on January 10 and she is obsessed with dinosaurs. Her birthday party is at our house on the Saturday before, about twelve kids plus a few parents.
A dinosaur dig party suits her: toy fossils buried in a sandbox, party food named after dinosaurs, and an explorer hat for each guest. With twelve kids, two adults running the dig keeps it calm.
She wants a volcano cake for the party. How do I make one?

Stack two round chocolate cakes, carve the top into a cone, cover it with chocolate frosting, and pour warm red and orange candy melts over the top so they run down like lava. A sparkler at the end gets the big reaction.
We host the family at our place most Saturdays. My sister Dana brings her twins, Leo and Sam, and their whole family is vegetarian, so every Saturday menu needs a vegetarian main.
Got it: a full vegetarian main for Dana, Leo and Sam at every Saturday gathering, not just side dishes.
My father-in-law Frank comes too. He uses a wheelchair, so we eat at the big table rather than on the patio.
Noted. Seating at the big table and everything on the ground floor so Frank can join.
I am training for the Las Vegas half marathon on March 14. I run on Tuesday and Thursday mornings before work and do my long run on Sunday. Can you build me a training plan?
A 16-week plan: Tuesday easy 5 km building to 8 km, Thursday intervals or tempo, Sunday long run from 8 km adding about 1 km a week up to 18 km, then a taper. Every fourth week is lighter.
My right knee gets sore after any run longer than 12 km. It is fine the next day.

Soreness that clears by the next day is a load issue, not an injury. Cap long runs at 12 km for two weeks, add 10 minutes of hip and quad strength work after Tuesday runs, and add no more than 1 km a week to the Sunday long run.
How do I keep the training going when I travel for work?
On a travel week keep Tuesday and Thursday as short easy runs wherever you are, and move the long run to a day you are home. Missing one long run does not hurt the plan.
I am flying to Tokyo for work from January 12 to January 16. Meetings are at our partner's office in Shinagawa all week, and I want to bring gifts for the team there.
Something from your home region, nicely wrapped, works well: small packaged treats for the team and something more personal for your main contact.
My main contact is Kenji. He collects whisky, and I want to spend about fifty dollars on his gift.
A small-batch American whisky in the fifty-dollar range, in a gift box, suits Kenji, since Japanese whisky is easy for him to get at home.
I am staying at a hotel near Shinagawa station and want to keep running during the trip.
To keep your training on track in Tokyo, run early along the canal path near Shinagawa station, which local runners use every morning; most hotels there have a small gym.
My mother-in-law Rosa speaks only Spanish, and we are visiting her in Guadalajara in late February. After three months of Duolingo I am at about A2, and I want to hold a real conversation with her.
Practise speaking out loud about the things you will actually discuss with Rosa. Fifteen minutes a day of that beats another hour of app exercises.
Rosa loves cooking and gardening, and she always asks about Mia.
Then prepare three short stories in Spanish: Mia's dinosaur phase, something you cooked, and a question about Rosa's garden. Rehearse them until they feel natural.
I work from home on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, and my lower back hurts after long days at the desk. I just bought a standing desk.
Alternate roughly forty minutes sitting and twenty standing, elbows at ninety degrees, monitor at eye level, and take a short walk every hour.
I want to use the home-office days for the strength work my running plan needs. I have a mat and a kettlebell at home.
On your home days do ten minutes of hip bridges, side planks and kettlebell deadlifts at lunch; it helps both the lower back and the knee stability your running plan asked for.
